proposal.summary: A heap buffer overflow in ClamAV's HFS+ partition file parser in affected versions may allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code or crash the scanning process by submitting a crafted HFS+ partition file.
proposal.affected_product: ClamAV versions 1.0.0 and earlier, 0.105.1 and earlier, and 0.103.7 and earlier
proposal.cwe_quote: This vulnerability is due to a missing buffer size check that may result in a heap buffer overflow write.

AV.quote: An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted HFS+ partition file to be scanned by ClamAV on an affected device.

PR.quote: An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted HFS+ partition file to be scanned by ClamAV on an affected device.

C.quote: A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the ClamAV scanning process

A.quote: or else crash the process, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Obtain and analyze the referenced ClamAV advisory/blog post, reproduce the issue against specified versions, and determine patched versions or mitigations; coordinate disclosure and prepare updates for affected packages.

evidence_quotes.quote: A vulnerability in the HFS+ partition file parser of ClamAV versions 1.0.0 and earlier, 0.105.1 and earlier, and 0.103.7 and earlier could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code.
This vulnerability is due to a missing buffer size check that may result in a heap buffer overflow write.
An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted HFS+ partition file to be scanned by ClamAV on an affected device.
A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the ClamAV scanning process
or else crash the process, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.
